text: This is Wayzo. You drop in a ticket, and your whole trip sorts itself out.
Planning a trip with friends is fun until someone asks: which hotel did we book? In this video I'll show you what I'm building, what already works, and what's coming next.
I'm Mirage, and I'm building Wayzo in public. It's a web app for group trips: one place for every ticket, stay and plan, so nobody has to dig through emails and screenshots again.
Right now a group trip lives in about nine apps. Email, the airline app, booking sites, screenshots, notes, a spreadsheet. Wayzo puts it in one trip.
And you know this chat. Which hotel? What time is the flight? Who's paying for the train?
Most travel apps ask where you want to go. But your group already booked.
So Wayzo starts from what you already have: your bookings.
Here's the landing page. The idea is simple: upload your tickets, tell us your vibe, and travel easy.
Step one, upload tickets. Step two, everyone shares their vibe: budget, food, pace. Step three, Wayzo builds the plan.
Let's try it for real. I'll create an account: name, email, password. Then a quick onboarding, just my home city, and I'm in.
Signing out and back in works too. Your trips are waiting for you.
Now a new trip. I'll call it Lisbon with friends, search for Lisbon, add the dates and pick euros. And here's the dashboard, empty for now, waiting for tickets.
This is the part I'm most excited about. I drop in the flight PDF. The AI reads it: flight number, date, time, from London to Lisbon, seats, price. I didn't type anything.
It also works with a screenshot. Here's the train ticket from Lisbon to Porto, straight from a phone.
And the hotel booking: check-in, check-out, the address and the price.
Everything lands on the right day of the trip. That's the dashboard filling itself.
Now, what's coming next. Every friend takes a short quiz: where they like to stay, what they eat, how fast they travel.
Then Wayzo suggests stays that fit the whole group, and you vote.
A day-by-day plan you can edit, with real places, and you can ask the AI to add a spot.
Shared expenses, so you always know who owes whom.
A seven AM brief every morning with the day's plan and the weather.
And later, Wayzo on WhatsApp.
That's episode one. I'm building this in public, so subscribe if you want to see what ships next. See you in the next one.
If you've ever lost a booking in a group chat, tell me in the comments. I read all of them.
